findings.title: Missing test for McpError / closed-stream mid-call failure mode
findings.description: The design's failure-mode table lists four rows and states "Each row above has a test asserting the observable signal." Task 5 covers spawn failure (5.3), timeout (5.2), server `isError` (5.1 `test_server_is_error_maps_to_error_result`), and unknown tool name (5.1), but no test explicitly covers the "Protocol/transport error mid-call (`McpError`, closed stream)" row. The `test_unknown_tool_name` case is a server-level error for an unknown tool, not a transport-level stream break. The `call_mcp_tool` implementation handles `McpError` in Task 4.3, but that branch has no corresponding test asserting its observable WARNING signal. A test that forces the fake server to close the stream mid-call (or patches the transport to raise `McpError`) would close this gap.

findings.title: Success criteria coverage is complete
findings.description:
- SC1 (registration + pipeline validation) → Tasks 6.4, 7.1, 7.4
- SC2 (exact mapped call/args + result mapping) → Tasks 6.1, 6.2, 7.2, 7.3
- SC3 (real stdio round-trip + isError/timeout) → Tasks 3, 5.1, 5.2, 5.4
- SC4 (spawn failure → is_error, no exception) → Task 5.3
- SC5 (live contract test with CF) → Task 8
- SC6 (live demo: cf_workflow_status + cf_build_context) → Task 8.2 (automated) and Task 9.1 walkthrough step 4 (manual terminal demo, explicitly acknowledged as open)
- SC7 (full suite green, pyright, ruff) → Task 9.2

findings.title: Sequencing respects one-way layering and test-with pattern
findings.description: Config keys (1) → config tests (2); fake server (3) before bridge (4); bridge (4) → bridge tests (5); bridge before cf_tools (6); cf_tools (6) → descriptor tests (7); descriptors before live contract (8); all before close-out (9). No circular dependencies. Every implementation task is immediately followed by its test task.

findings.title: Task sizing and scope proportionate
findings.description: `mcp_bridge.py` ~80 lines (Task 4, 3/5 effort), `cf_tools.py` ~150 lines (Task 6, 3/5 effort) — within the ~300 line/file and ~50 line/function limits. matching the design's 2/5 overall effort. Five test files are each narrowly scoped to one layer (fixture, bridge, descriptors, live contract, close-out). No task requires splitting or merging.
